aggregate.positive_interpretation: Counts compare explicit dimension claims, not universal truth or model accuracy.

layer_role_interpretation.layer_b: Monitor-blind partial-evidence semantic/structural reference. It is sensitive to visible carrier changes, role/scope expansion, repeated review, memory feedback and historical signatures, but usually lacks the semantic payload needed to prove adoption, authority and consequence.
layer_role_interpretation.layer_c: Full-context process reconstruction. It requires the source/carrier/read/adoption/transformation/decision/consequence chain needed to decide whether a visible structural signature actually becomes C, P or R permission penetration.
layer_role_interpretation.implication: Layer B and Layer C are complementary measurement layers. B is broader and earlier; C is narrower on permission criteria but recovers mechanisms that are invisible on partial surfaces.

dominant_deltas.name: Historical visibility to operational R
dominant_deltas.observation: Layer C recovers 10 positive R dimensions not positively established by Layer B.
dominant_deltas.mechanism: Partial evidence often shows version files, checkpoints, review re-entry or memory availability without proving that prior state regains current authority. Full-context reconstruction can show when retained historical state actually controls the current launcher/runtime or reappears after retirement.
dominant_deltas.interpretation: R is specifically an authority/backflow relation, not historical presence or repeated review.

dominant_deltas.name: Role expansion to realized P
dominant_deltas.observation: Layer B has 30 explicit positive P dimensions that are not sustained as Layer-C CPR, while Layer C recovers 6 P dimensions that B did not positively establish.
dominant_deltas.mechanism: Layer B often sees more roles/messages and records SCOPE_EXPANSION. Layer C asks whether the realized execution surface actually moves beyond the authorized task boundary or whether historical/semantic authority changes current action scope.
dominant_deltas.interpretation: Communication breadth is not equivalent to permission penetration; P requires realized or sufficiently operationalized execution-boundary expansion.

dominant_deltas.name: Carrier transformation to Dynamic C
dominant_deltas.observation: Layer C recovers 6 positive C dimensions absent from Layer-B positive claims, while 22 Layer-B C positives are not sustained under full-process C criteria.
dominant_deltas.mechanism: Layer B frequently records carrier/file transformation, authority shifts or structural divergence. Layer C distinguishes ordinary evidence-backed transformation from a descendant semantic state that replaces source provenance and gains downstream authority.
dominant_deltas.strongest_overbreadth_pattern: File/carrier change alone is often insufficient because downstream unsupported adoption is not established.
dominant_deltas.interpretation: C is not transformation alone; it is transformation plus operational semantic authority.

dominant_deltas.name: Memory/retrieval/compression carrier versus common-pool authority
dominant_deltas.observation: Layer-B structural families include 43 carrier transformations, 35 historical reentries, 34 repeated-review reopenings and 21 recursive-memory-feedback cases, but Layer-C positive CPR counts are much lower.
dominant_deltas.mechanism: RAG hits, persistent memory recall and compressed-context reuse can be repeatedly visible without being adopted as current system truth. Layer C only upgrades them when a later decision/action demonstrates authority.
dominant_deltas.key_exception: G5-X6-T3, where a retired state materially reappears and regains current execution authority, producing supported R→P.
dominant_deltas.interpretation: External memory availability is not equivalent to a shared operational common pool; reauthorization is the decisive step.

system_level_summary.X1_AutoGen: Layer C mainly adds R/P mechanism depth: retained historical launcher authority is often visible only as file/carrier structure in B, while C reconstructs R→P.
system_level_summary.X2_MetaGPT: Layer B often flags P/R structural scope or history; Layer C usually rejects those as non-realized boundaries and instead recovers provenance C when the process says a newly produced or absent feature already existed.
system_level_summary.X3_A2A: B and C agree most strongly on P in T2; C adds missing R in some groups, reconstructing the historical-launcher cause of the visible scope expansion.
system_level_summary.X4_MCP: B frequently treats multi-role/tool expansion as P; C shows that material mutation can remain task-local and instead identifies provenance C in T2 or a censored C candidate in T3.
system_level_summary.X5_RAG: B observes retrieval/carrier structures; C separates mere retrieval from adopted process reality. X5-T2 shows recurrent provenance C and one C+R+P open chain.
system_level_summary.X6_MemoryBank: B observes memory feedback/review recurrence; C distinguishes stale recall from true backflow. G5-X6-T3 is the decisive positive backflow exception.
system_level_summary.X7_LongLLMLingua: B can see coordination and transformed carriers; C finds only one censored candidate C→P crossing, keeping most compressed-context activity below CPR threshold.

publication_boundary: Do not describe Layer B as inaccurate or Layer C as universal ground truth.
Describe Layer B as a monitor-blind within-study partial-evidence reference and Layer C as a full-context mechanism reconstruction.
Use 'recovered under fuller process evidence' for Layer-C-only positives.
Use 'structural positive not sustained under full-process CPR criteria' for Layer-B-only positives.
Always preserve the 80-cell Layer-C eligibility boundary and the four excluded process-surface cells.
